newsitem.title: GERMANY: Thyssen official optimistic on Transrapid.
newsitem.headline: Thyssen official optimistic on Transrapid.

text.p: Eckhard Rohkamm, head of Thyssen Industrie, the company leading the consortium charged with leading Germany's Transrapid rail project said on Wednesday he remained optimistic that the project would come into being.
"I personally am still optimistic that we shall have Transrapid on the Hamburg-Berlin route," he said.
Rohkamm denied a report in the Handelsblatt newspaper on Wednesday suggesting that the consortium thought that the project would not be commercially sustainable.
"There has been no final appraisal of the costs of the project or of the potential receipts," he told a news briefing before a regular meeting of the consortium members.
Rohkamm added that the results of a study of the commercial viability of the project would likely be known in late March or early April.
Earlier Handelsblatt newspaper reported that the future of the project was in jeopardy.
Handelsblatt said new projections showed that Transrapid would have to charge much higher fares than previously believed, making it uneconomic. The newspaper did not cite the source of its new data.
A government study analysing the costs and viability of the rail project, planned to run between Berlin and Hamburg, is due for release at the end of March.
